rationale: Exercise the accepted cold-cache discriminator using actual saved bytes and one reported read error; permit proper error propagation and measure preservation on successful completion.

feedback.answered: The persisted-log interface and suffix-merge expectation ground prefix preservation on reported append success. Close/reopen supplies the cold-cache history without mutating cache state. The selected shard entry is the actual callee of ShardedDB.SaveRaftStateCtx; context reset/destruction and backend close/reopen duties are included in the fixed driver.
remaining: Actual fault delivery, returned append status and persisted prefix must be observed by the trusted runner.
Physical fault production and whole-cluster consequences are outside the local obligation.
feedback.rationale: The fixed driver preserves the original read-error/cache-miss premise and measures stored bytes independently from the return value.

candidate.rationale: The persistent-store interface and explicit prefix-retention test ground a success-conditioned preservation duty. Error rejection is allowed; read failure alone is not a violation.

question.question: When an unaligned batched-log append needs a previously persisted prefix after a cache miss, can a KV read error be treated as absence and cause a successful write to discard that prefix?
question.importance: Silent loss of previously stored log entries can invalidate recovery and replication history. The immediate subject is persistence semantics; no cluster-level data-loss endpoint has been executed.
contexts: Unaligned append in an existing batch
Explicit read error, with stored bytes still present
event_paths: engine SaveRaftState -> db.saveRaftState -> recordBatch -> getMergedFirstBatch -> cache miss/GetValue -> CommitWriteBatch -> read persisted batch

supporting_behavior_ids.B-persistence: Engine treats a returned SaveRaftState error as fatal, so swallowed error bypasses caller handling.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-formation: Stored entry history constrains commitment/replication in the A1 relationship supported by this storage question.

counterevidence: A cache hit avoids GetValue, so a simple hot-cache append would not exercise this premise.
Aligned batch replacement requires no old prefix.
The engine panics on a returned persistence error; a check must distinguish proper rejection from successful destructive replacement.
question.trigger_rationale: Pebble GetValue explicitly returns non-not-found errors, but batch lookup discards their cause and merge treats false as no old data. A clean reopen plus one read failure discriminates this from the protective cache path; source lookup is more valuable than ambiguous result-buffer mutation.

obligation.description: If saving a strictly appended log suffix reports success, previously successfully persisted entries preceding that suffix must remain intact unless explicitly removed by a snapshot or compaction operation. A failed lookup of their existing batch must not turn a successful append into implicit prefix deletion.

scope.description: Batched LogDB shard storage preservation across an unaligned append after close/reopen with one reported non-not-found KV lookup error.
assumptions: Earlier entries were successfully saved and verified after reopening the same backend.
Incoming entry 4 strictly follows existing entries 1 through 3 within one batch; there is no snapshot, truncation request, compaction or concurrent writer.
The single read fault returns an error before invoking the GetValue callback and does not change stored bytes; subsequent backend calls operate normally.
The implication is conditioned on saveRaftState returning nil; a returned error does not violate this success-conditioned property.
excluded: Whole-cluster data loss or consensus safety endpoint
Actual filesystem fault production and crash durability
Non-batched format and unrelated backend faults

grounding.derivation: ILogDB persistently stores Raft history and SaveRaftState atomically saves the supplied update. The merge test explicitly retains earlier indexes when replacing a later suffix. This check only appends, so deleting earlier entries is not part of its update. IKVStore/Pebble allow a returned read error distinct from absence; caller error propagation is a valid outcome. Prefix preservation on reported success follows independently of any promise to succeed under a read fault.
grounding.applicability: The obligation is local to the actual shard implementation reached by ShardedDB.SaveRaftStateCtx, not a claim that a cluster-level failure was reached.

associations.rationale: This path replaces the batch containing the old prefix and incoming suffix; a successful append must preserve earlier entries.

bindings.description: Merges the first batch, updates the cache, serializes entries and puts the replacement batch into the atomic write batch.
